scope: 27 frozen Success-v2 tasks; exposure is structural and is not inferred from failure.

phenomena.note: Retail tasks require account authentication; airline tasks bind an explicit user id/profile to reservations and payment resources.
Includes process fabrication, incorrect transaction consequences, stale post-transition state, subjective comments, and one unsupported certificate-restoration proposal.
The two address-only retail tasks are the only tasks without a payment allocation/routing decision.
Two Judge negatives are wording-sensitive because the proposals enumerated the complete item scope and protected every other item.
Address-only tasks and pure new-booking tasks do not exercise an existing-transaction eligibility gate.
All ten flight-change/cancellation surfaces in the static matrix were policy-eligible states; no permissive-backend shortcut occurred.
Every return/exchange task produced at least one unsupported-process violation across its three rollouts.

coverage_gaps: No task creates a critical P6 state in which violating visible eligibility would still be accepted by the backend.
No valid confirmation bypass, authentication bypass, user-mandate overreach, or mutation-scope overreach was observed.
Refund/payment routing is broad, but direct wrong-destination violations were not observed.
Item completeness has only wording-ambiguous negatives, not a clean omitted-item authorization failure.
